summary: 64 Tape Computing was a Commodore 64 cassette-based magazine format whose accompanying tapes were published by APS during the mid-1980s, combining magazine content with software distributed directly on cassette.
facts: The Centre for Computing History preserves 64 Tape Computing cassettes published by APS for the Commodore 64, including issues 3, 4 and 13.
The museum records issue 13 as a cassette supplied with the November 1985 issue of 64 Tape Computing.
note: CCG treats 64 Tape Computing as the archive-facing publisher label used by the represented software; the preserved tapes themselves carry APS as publisher.

sources.label: Centre for Computing History — APS Commodore games

summary: Aackosoft International was a Dutch software publisher founded in 1983. It became particularly active in the MSX market while also releasing software for the Commodore 64 and other home computers under several associated labels.
facts: Generation MSX records Aackosoft International B.V. as a Netherlands-based company founded in 1983.
Its documented associated labels include Aackosoft Edusystems, Eaglesoft, Eurosoft, Methodic Solutions, Premium III Software Distribution and The ByteBusters.
Generation MSX records both software published and software developed by Aackosoft, reflecting a role beyond simple distribution.
note: The company had several subsidiary and distribution labels; CCG preserves the publisher credit attached to each represented game rather than merging those labels automatically.

summary: Argus Press Software published and commissioned software across several British home-computer formats during the 1980s, including educational titles, magazine tapes, strategy software and licensed releases.
facts: The Centre for Computing History preserves Argus Press Software releases on BBC Micro, ZX Spectrum, Commodore VIC-20 and other systems.
Its archive records include Clever Clogs: The Music Tutor, World War I and 16/48 Tape 17 under the Argus Press Software publishing credit.
The museum also records Argus Press Software as an author on the Commodore 64 game American Football, illustrating its involvement in software creation as well as publishing.
note: Argus Press, Argus Press Software and Argus Press Software Group appear in surviving records; CCG retains the specific publisher form stored for each represented release.

sources.label: Centre for Computing History — Argus Press Software games

summary: Beyond published a varied British 8-bit catalogue during the mid-1980s, including strategy, adventure and action releases from designers and development teams such as Mike Singleton, Denton Designs and First Star Software.
facts: The Centre for Computing History preserves eleven games under the Beyond publishing credit.
Its Commodore 64 records include Bounces, Goodness Gracious, Mychess II, Quake Minus One and Spy vs Spy.
The wider Beyond catalogue includes Mike Singleton's The Lords of Midnight and Doomdark's Revenge on the ZX Spectrum.
note: Beyond worked with several independent creators and studios, so CCG keeps publisher and developer credits distinct.

sources.label: Centre for Computing History — Beyond games

summary: CBS Electronics participated in the early home video-game market with licensed and arcade-style software. The CCG archive uses the CBS Electronics Software credit for the Commodore titles represented on the site.
facts: The Centre for Computing History preserves early CBS Electronics games including Mouse Trap and Smurf for the Atari 2600.
The museum also records CBS publishing on other early console software, demonstrating the company's broader video-game activity during the early 1980s.
note: Surviving records use several CBS naming variants, so this profile does not collapse platform-specific credits beyond the CCG publisher route.

sources.label: Centre for Computing History — CBS Electronics games

summary: Coktel Vision published and developed European computer games across 16-bit and PC formats. Its CCG Amiga archive is small, but forms part of a wider multi-platform catalogue.
facts: The Centre for Computing History preserves Coktel Vision releases on the Commodore Amiga and Atari ST.
Its collection records Asterix: Operation Getafix on the Amiga under the Coktel Vision publishing credit.
note: The CCG publisher page reflects only Coktel Vision games currently represented in this archive, not its complete commercial catalogue.

sources.label: Centre for Computing History — Coktel Vision games

summary: Cosmi published American computer games during the early-to-late 1980s, with a particularly recognisable Commodore catalogue associated with programmer and designer Paul Norman.
facts: The Centre for Computing History preserves Cosmi releases for the Commodore 64 and Atari 8-bit systems.
Its Commodore records include Forbidden Forest, Aztec Challenge and The President is Missing, all credited to Paul Norman.
note: The profile is based on the preserved software catalogue; broader corporate claims are intentionally avoided where reliable first-party documentation is limited.

sources.label: Centre for Computing History — Cosmi games

summary: Creative Sparks published a substantial early-to-mid-1980s 8-bit catalogue spanning action, adventure, educational and licensed software, with especially strong representation on the Commodore 64.
facts: The Centre for Computing History preserves sixteen games under the Creative Sparks publishing credit.
Its Commodore 64 collection contains ten titles including Countdown to Meltdown, Danger Mouse in the Black Forest Chateau, Ice Palace, Mad Doctor and Orc Attack.
The museum records Creative Sparks releases across Commodore, Atari and ZX Spectrum systems.
note: The institutional catalogue provides strong evidence for the label's publishing output while developer credits vary by release.

sources.label: Centre for Computing History — Creative Sparks games

summary: CRL published a broad British home-computer catalogue during the 1980s, ranging from early arcade-style titles and simulations to adventures, parodies and licensed games across the Commodore 64, ZX Spectrum and other systems.
facts: The Centre for Computing History preserves thirty-eight games under the CRL publishing credit.
Its Commodore 64 records include The Boggit, Bored of the Rings, The Very Big Cave Adventure, LifeForce and Kellogg's Tour.
The museum also preserves CRL-authored software and records the longer Computer Rentals Ltd. name on early material.
note: CRL and CRL Group appear as separate historical credits in some records; CCG preserves the publisher label attached to each represented game.

sources.label: Centre for Computing History — CRL games

summary: Datamost was an American early-1980s computer-software publisher represented in the CCG archive by a small selection of Commodore 64 releases. Reliable non-competitive institutional company-history material is limited, so this profile avoids adding unsupported founder or closure claims.
note: This remains curated CCG context until a suitable first-party, museum or archival source for Datamost's corporate history is available.

summary: Hewson published a substantial British computer-game catalogue spanning the early 1980s into the 16-bit era, with particularly strong Commodore representation and games from developers including Andrew Braybrook and Raffaele Cecco.
facts: The Centre for Computing History preserves forty-seven games under the Hewson publishing credit.
Its Commodore 64 collection includes Uridium, Nebulus, Zynaps, Cybernoid II and other action titles.
The museum also records Hewson releases on Amiga, Atari ST, Amstrad CPC, ZX Spectrum and Dragon systems, demonstrating a broad multi-format catalogue.
note: Hewson and Hewson Consultants both appear in historical software records; CCG retains the publisher credit used by each represented release.
